The core issue arises in evaluating nested marginal sums within causal trees. When computing P(Y|do(x)), the front-door path involves two levels of summation: outer over M and inner over X. In `evalTree`, assigning `a = {...assign, [v]: val}` causes the inner grid point for X to overwrite any previously assigned value from the outer context. This leads to incorrect conditional probability evaluations. Specifically, P(M|X)@d requires M to be in sumCtx (outer sum), so it evaluates using the intervention value of X, whereas P(X|)@d requires X to be in sumCtx (inner sum), thus evaluating at the grid point. To resolve this, we must isolate variable names or track summed variables to correctly apply either prior or intervened values depending on context. The error manifests as double-subtraction in mean adjustments due to misapplication of regression terms. Correctly distinguishing these contexts ensures valid front-door estimands.
